target_customer: Local businesses in Mexico and Latin America, mainly restaurants, selling directly to consumers and wanting to avoid marketplace commissions
problem: Delivery marketplaces took roughly 25 to 30 percent of each sale; Pidedirecto offers online ordering, logistics orchestration and point of sale for a fixed monthly fee.
business_model: B2B SaaS with fixed monthly fee and delivery orchestration that connects couriers from Rappi, Uber and Didi or the merchant's own drivers
product_category: Restaurant ordering, point of sale and delivery logistics platform

founders.name: Hussein Fawzi
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; background not stated.

founders.name: Ronni Samir Sulaka
founders.background_notes: Listed with a profile on the YC page.

founders.name: Anders Steiner
founders.background_notes: YC profile says 15 years in tech and open source contributions.

competitors.name: Uber Eats
competitors.what: Delivery marketplace charging restaurants high commissions
competitors.traction_then: 47,262 users in Mexico in the first half of 2021 per a Fintonic study cited by the source

competitors.name: Rappi
competitors.what: Delivery marketplace with restaurant commissions around 30 percent before temporary cuts
competitors.traction_then: Cut Mexican restaurant fees temporarily in early 2021 after CANIRAC complaints

competitors.name: DiDi Food
competitors.traction_then: Named with Uber Eats and Rappi as the main apps in Mexico in 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Online ordering, point of sale and courier dispatch integrations across several fleets; standard engineering with integration complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Restaurants that adopt point of sale and ordering stay, but ordering software and delivery orchestration were easy to copy and Rappi is both a partner and a rival channel.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The marketplaces cut fees temporarily in 2021 but no copy or acquisition was found; Rappi became a certification partner on the company site.

market_need_then: Mexican restaurants complained of commissions near 30 percent and CANIRAC said pre-pandemic fees were unsustainable (January 2021); founders told TechCrunch customers lost 25 to 30 percent of each sale to marketplaces.

branding.domain_note: Uses pidedirecto.mx, a country domain; the name is also used in other Latin American markets.

identity.voice_and_tone: Spanish copy about delivering in record time, positioned against commissions

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive Spanish name that means order direct; no press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Pide Directo raised a 5.25 million dollar seed in October 2021 led by JAM FUND and grew to about 150 staff, with a claimed 5,000 clients and a Rappi partnership. It pitched fixed-fee software against 25 to 30 percent marketplace commissions. No later priced round, exit or shutdown was found, so growth since 2021 is funded either by revenue or undisclosed capital.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch, Contxto and El Referente summaries; investor lists differ across trackers (VC Backed lists Trajectory and Flucas Ventures). An aggregator lists a 350,000 dollar seed in February 2021 and another dates a 5.3 million seed to February 2022; both are single unverified claims. Total raised ranges 5.3 to 5.6 million across aggregators. HQ shown as Monterrey on YC and Mexico City elsewhere. Competitors are the delivery marketplaces whose commissions were the problem, from a January 2021 source; direct restaurant software rivals were not found in dated sources. Founder education and prior employers not stated on sources opened. The site claims Rappi Top Tech Partner status.
